output.findings: Claude Shannon was born on April 30, 1916, in Petoskey, Michigan, U.S., and died on February 24, 2001, in Medford, Massachusetts, at the age of 84. His key contributions to information theory include his master's thesis, "A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits," which demonstrated the application of Boolean algebra to simplify digital circuit design. He is most renowned for his 1948 paper, "A Mathematical Theory of Communication," which laid the theoretical foundations for the entire field of information theory, introducing concepts like entropy, redundancy, and channel capacity. Furthermore, Shannon formally introduced and popularized the term "bit" as the fundamental unit of information, a concept central to digital computing and communication.
